newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish farm losses seen at PLN 1 bln - minister.
newsitem.headline: Polish farm losses seen at PLN 1 bln - minister.

text.p: The cost of lost crops and land recultivation in the flooded regions of southern and western Poland may reach one billion zlotys, the agriculture minister said on Thursday.
"We estimate a total of 370,000-400,000 hectares have been flooded...and the losses over the (flooded) area may amount to about one billion zlotys," Jaroslaw Kalinowski told a news conference.
Kalinowski upheld his earlier estimate that the loss of grain crops might amount to 800,000 tonnes and stressed it should not destabilise the grains market.
"We estimate that due to the flooding we have lost 600,000-800,000 tonnes of grain. It is a substantial amount but it will not lead to destabilising grain market," the minister added.
Analysts said that apart from the devastated grain fields heavy losses resulted from the flooding of fruit plantations and orchards which would require large financial support.
Kalinowski excluded the possibility of emergency grain imports unless heavy rains occur during harvest-time.

"Harvest is about to begin, crop output forecast is good, and if there are no heavy rains then there is nothing to worry about and there will be no necessity of grain imports," Kalinowski told Reuters.
Early in July Kalinowski forecast this year crop output at 23.5-24.0 million tonnes, with the grain of low quality.

Analysts of the government-funded Agriculture Economy Institute said the grain losses would amount to 500,000-800,000 tonnes, which means that this-year crop output would range from 23.6 to 24.7 million tonnes.
In 1996 Poland's grain output amounted to 24.7 million tonnes and country's grain reserves are estimated at around four million tonnes.
The country's 1997 demand for grains is estimated to amount to 26.2 million tonnes.
